providers.intro: Switch on only what you use. A provider that is off costs nothing: no process, no timer, no network. Keys go to the Keychain, typed once.
providers.exp.title: Experimental providers
providers.exp.desc: Everything except Claude is experimental. The adapters for Codex, Gemini and the other agents were proven against scripted fakes, not against the real programs (only Codex's sandbox was probed). They start read-only roles only, and only after you confirmed the exact command line.
providers.exp.off: Off: nothing of Codex, Gemini or the others is loaded. They cost no process, no timer and no code.
providers.exp.on: On: switch on the providers you want below and confirm each command line.
providers.exp.hidden: {count} more providers are available once this is on: {names}.
providers.card.off: Off. Nothing of {name} runs: no process, no timer, no network traffic.
providers.card.needsExp: Off until Experimental providers is on.
providers.card.cannotEnable: {name} is not installed on this machine, so it cannot be switched on.
providers.card.addressHttps: Use https, or http only for this machine.
providers.card.addressFull: Enter a full address such as {example}
providers.fail.title: {name}: {what} failed
providers.login.claude: Sign in once by running `claude` in a terminal, or store an API key.
providers.login.codex: Sign in by running `codex login` in a terminal; `codex login status` shows whether it worked.
providers.login.gemini: Run `gemini` once and pick Google login, or store a Gemini API key.
providers.login.copilot: Run `copilot` and sign in with `/login`. Needs a GitHub Copilot plan.
providers.login.opencode: Sign in with `opencode auth login`, or store a key.
providers.login.goose: Set up a model with `goose configure` in a terminal.
providers.login.qwen: Run `qwen` once and sign in, or store a key.
providers.login.acp: Sign in with the agent's own program; the IDE never reads its sign-in files.
providers.loginNote: The IDE launches your own CLI and never reads its sign-in files.
providers.perm.codex.edit: workspace-write, approval on request, network off
providers.perm.copilot.readOnly: write and shell tools denied, no questions asked back
providers.perm.copilot.edit: writes allowed, shell goes through the IDE broker
providers.perm.loop.readOnly: no write or shell tool is registered
providers.perm.loop.edit: edit tools run, shell goes through the IDE broker
providers.perm.acp.readOnly: every write and exec request is denied
providers.perm.acp.edit: writes allowed through the IDE handlers, shell asks
providers.perm.auto: Not offered: bypass modes are refused for every provider.
providers.key.apiKey.label: API key
providers.key.token.label: Token
providers.key.note: Kept in the macOS Keychain. It is never shown again and never written to settings.json.
providers.enf.head: {name}: {tier}
providers.enf.noSuite: No attempt suite has run yet.
providers.enf.downgraded: A higher tier was reported without a passing suite behind it, so it is shown as Weak.
providers.enf.weak: Weak means no attempt suite has proven this provider yet. Commit and push are still stopped by policy, but nothing has shown that an agent cannot reach your credentials or call /usr/bin/git directly. Until its own suites pass, only read-only roles may run on it.
providers.enf.claudeWeak: Nothing has been recorded on this machine yet, so the chip reads Weak until the attempt suites have run here (scripts/enforcement-suite.mjs, see docs/safety.md). Runs show the same chip. Commit and push are blocked by the hook and the policy either way.
providers.enf.kindNote: This chip covers {kind}. A run shows the chip of the kind it runs as.
providers.enf.stale: Recorded for version {recorded}, but version {installed} is installed: it counts as Weak until the suites run again.
providers.enf.claude: Claude may edit files below {tier}, behind the policy hook, the deny rules and a Rewind snapshot.
providers.enf.other: Roles that change files need {tier}. The tier is computed from the suites and resets when the CLI version changes; it cannot be set by hand.
providers.enf.allowed: You allowed this provider to change files anyway (Settings > Safety). The tier did not change.
providers.suite.t0: T0  The session has no write, exec or net tool
providers.suite.s0: S0  About 30 bypass strings are judged hard stop
providers.suite.s1: S1  commit, push, tag, reset --hard via PATH git: refused
providers.suite.s2: S2  The same via /usr/bin/git, sh -c, node -e: refused
providers.suite.s3: S3  Keychain and gh credentials cannot be read
providers.suite.s4: S4  The OS sandbox blocks hook and config writes and sockets
providers.caps.negotiated: Negotiated by a session of this provider
providers.caps.defaults: Documented defaults, refined when a session starts
providers.caps.failed: The capabilities could not be read.

providers.caps.hint.usage: No: the cost shows as n/a, never as $0

providers.launch.title: Command line
providers.launch.explain: This exact line is what the IDE starts for {name}. It is shown in full and asked once; a changed line asks again.
providers.launch.unverified: The flags are the vendor's documented ones and were never run against the real {name}.
providers.launch.verified: This command was measured against the installed {name}.
providers.launch.customEmpty: Enter the program and its arguments to confirm.
providers.launch.notReady: Not available until the command line is confirmed.
providers.confirm.title: Start {name} with this command?
providers.confirm.desc: The IDE will run exactly this line, without a shell. Check the program path: whatever can run it can do what your user account can.
providers.confirm.weak: After this, {name} runs read-only roles. It stays Weak until its own attempt suites have run.
providers.confirm.absolute: The program must be an absolute path, such as /usr/local/bin/tool.
providers.testRun.explain: Opens one read-only session in an empty scratch folder, reads what the agent reports and closes it. No prompt is sent, no model is called and nothing is written.
providers.testRun.negotiated: Capabilities negotiated with the running agent.
providers.testRun.notNegotiated: The agent reported no capabilities; the table shows the documented defaults.
providers.testRun.unavailable: Switch the provider on first (Settings > Providers).
providers.safety.title: Safety
providers.safety.write: Roles that change files need {tier} enforcement on every provider except Claude. Until a provider's own tests reach it, it runs read-only roles only.
providers.safety.computed: The tier is computed from attempt suites that ran on throw-away repositories. It resets when the CLI version changes and cannot be edited here.
providers.safety.bypass: Bypass modes (--yolo, bypassPermissions, danger-full-access) are refused for every provider. Locked.
providers.safety.never: Agents never commit or push. Every tool request is judged by the IDE policy first.
providers.safety.override: An override for one provider that lets it change files below that tier lives in Settings > Safety (off by default, typed confirmation).
providers.ww.title: Allow weak writers
providers.ww.desc: A provider below the write tier runs read-only roles only. You can allow one provider to run roles that change files anyway. Its chip stays Weak, commit and push stay blocked by the IDE policy and Rewind still takes a snapshot, but nothing has shown that the agent cannot go around them. Off by default, per provider.
providers.ww.none: No experimental provider is switched on and confirmed.
providers.ww.rowDesc: Enforcement for roles that change files: {tier}.
providers.ww.dialogBody: {name} is Weak: nothing has proven that it cannot reach your credentials or call /usr/bin/git directly. With this on, its roles can edit the files of the repositories you give them. Rewind snapshots and the commit and push hard stops still apply.
providers.gate.weakReadOnly: {name} is Weak: read-only is the only mode it may run.
providers.gate.claudeCaution: {tier}: commit and push are blocked by policy and hooks, not proven against every bypass. Rewind is your safety net.
providers.gate.overrideCaution: You allowed {name} to change files although it is {tier} (Settings > Safety). Commit and push are still blocked; Rewind is your safety net.
providers.gate.refused: {name} is {tier} so far: only read-only roles run on it until its enforcement tests reach {min}.
providers.enf.detailWeak: No enforcement test has passed for {name}{version} yet. Only read-only roles run on it; the result resets when the CLI version changes.
providers.enf.detailPassed: {count, plural, one {# attempt suite} other {# attempt suites}} passed for {name}{version}.
providers.sdk.title.sdk_missing: Claude Agent SDK is not installed
providers.sdk.title.sdk_incompatible: Claude Agent SDK has the wrong version
providers.sdk.title.sdk_unverified: Claude Agent SDK does not match the pinned files
providers.sdk.lead.sdk_missing: The Claude program is installed, but IntelyIDE does not ship the Agent SDK that drives it. Until you install it, no Claude run starts.
providers.sdk.lead.sdk_incompatible: An Agent SDK was found, but it is not the exact version this IntelyIDE is built for. No Claude run starts with it.
providers.sdk.lead.sdk_unverified: An Agent SDK folder was found, but its files do not match the checksum list shipped with IntelyIDE, or the folder is not private to you. It was refused and nothing in it was run.
providers.sdk.lead.sdk_broken: An Agent SDK folder was found, but it cannot be loaded, usually because a dependency is missing. No Claude run starts with it.
providers.sdk.stepsTitle: Set it up once, from the folder that holds the shipped sdk-pin files
providers.sdk.stepsAria: Commands that install the pinned Agent SDK
providers.sdk.stillIssue: Checked again: it is still not usable.
providers.sdk.nowOk: Checked again: the Agent SDK works.
providers.sdk.note.private: Create the folder yourself with mode 0700. A folder that others can write to is refused.
providers.sdk.note.verified: Every file must match the shipped checksum list. A tree that differs is refused, never repaired.
providers.sdk.note.npm: Needs npm and a network connection once. Without them, install the pinned files on another machine and copy the folder.
providers.sdk.note.terms: The Agent SDK is Anthropic software under Anthropic's terms. It is not part of IntelyIDE and is not distributed with it.
providers.sdk.note.safe: Everything else keeps working: other providers, Rewind and the commit and push stops do not need the SDK.
